title: Localized Segal-presheaf presentations of algebroids
statement:
Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid], [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] and [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor]. For small monoidal $C$, $P(C)$ with Day convolution is presentably monoidal. The presheaf category $P(C_\otimes)$ is presentable and has pointwise small colimits. Spaces admit small colimits and cartesian product of spaces preserves them separately. The full subcategory $Q_C$ is the presentable reflective localization at the labelled spine maps. For a monoidally compatible small set $S$, $P^S(C)$ is a monoidal reflective localization of $P(C)$ with strong monoidal reflector and lax monoidal fully faithful right adjoint. The category $Q_C^S$ is the presentable reflective localization of $Q_C$ at $L_CE_C(\phi)\to L_CE_C(\psi)$ for $(\phi\to\psi)\in S$.
There are natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Algd}(P(C))\simeq Q_C,\qquad\operatorname{Algd}(P^S(C))\simeq Q_C^S.$$
The first identifies the object space of an algebroid $A$ with $Z([0])$ and its mapping object $A(x,y)\in P(C)$ with $H_Z(x,y)$. For every $Z\in Q_C$ there is a natural equivalence of spaces over $Z([0])^2$
$$\operatorname{Map}_{P(C_\otimes)}(E_C(\phi),Z)\simeq\int_{(x,y)\in Z([0])^2}\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,H_Z(x,y)),$$
where the integral denotes the total space of the indicated family. Consequently $Z\in Q_C^S$ exactly when every $H_Z(x,y)$ is $S$-local; the second equivalence is the restriction of the first to these objects. The reflector $L_C^S$ keeps the object space and applies the coefficient reflector to each mapping object.
Every presentably monoidal infinity category $V$ has a strong monoidal presentation $V\simeq P^S(C)$ for small monoidal $C$ and monoidally compatible small $S$. For presentations $V\simeq P^S(C)$ and $W\simeq P^T(D)$, $S\odot T$ is monoidally compatible and
$$V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W\simeq P^{S\odot T}(C\times D).$$
Under the displayed algebroid equivalences, the bifunctor $\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)$ corresponds to
$$H(X,Y)=L_{C\times D}^{S\odot T}(i_C^SX\boxtimes i_D^TY).$$
For $S=T=\varnothing$, it corresponds to the external product of Segal presheaves itself. All these identifications are natural in coherent diagrams and on their canonical maps.
